newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon's Banque Audi buys local bank.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon's Banque Audi buys local bank.

text.p: Lebanon's Banque Audi, one of Lebanon's biggest banks, has bought medium-size Beirut bank Credit Commerciale du Moyen Orient (CCMO), banking sources said on Thursday.

"The rumours are true. The deal is done but we are still awating a final letter of approval from the central bank," a source said. "It is an acquisition that is definitely going to translate into an absorption," he added.

Banque Audi, one of three banks listed on the Beirut Stock Exchange, last week lost out to billionaire Saudi Sheikh Khalid bin Mahfouz in a race to buy Credit Libanais bank which has the largest retail banking network in Lebanon.
Credit Commercial du Moyen Orient has eight branches and is ranked among the Beta group of 16 Lebanese banks with deposits ranging from $75 million to $250 million.
"It is a very healthy bank with a very high financial standing," the source said. It had assets of some $300 million, a 0.9 percent market share and a 65.2 percent liquidity ratio, he added.

"This is real consolidation for the banking sector because you can talk of economies of scale and upsizing," the source added. Audi was expected to issue a communique on the acquisition later on Thursday, he said.
